chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mufaddal ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said to me: 'O Mufaddal! The one who exposes himself to an unjust ruler, and an affliction befalls him, he will not be rewarded for it, nor will he be granted patience for it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on suffering inflicted by an unjust ruler if one actively exposes oneself to them?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between obligatory patience (sabr) and voluntary suffering (balaya) incurred by seeking out unjust rulers without necessity. Shia scholars emphasize that while enduring a ruler's oppression is meritorious, actively exposing oneself to harm through one's own choice negates the spiritual reward, as the affliction is viewed as a consequence of personal agency rather than divine decree. This teaching underscores the principle of 'not throwing oneself into destruction' (la tulfu anfusakum) within the context of political quietism and strategic engagement.
